{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABXZ_KWA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhA-Fdw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 23, "title": "Support IndexNode, FrontFacingNode, ScreenNode and ViewportDepthNode", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 reference loader and exporter already support several shared Three.js TSL singleton nodes (such as `frontFacing` and `screenUV`), but ordinary independently constructed instances of useful geometry/screen-related node classes are not supported by the default serializer/resolver.

Extend the **existing plugins** to handle the next four agreed node classes when their behavior can be faithfully represented:

- `IndexNode`
- `FrontFacingNode`
- `ScreenNode`
- `ViewportDepthNode`

Keep the extension data-only and Three.js-first. Supporting exact shared exported objects is not equivalent to supporting arbitrary instances; preserve this distinction.

## Expected outcome

1. **Audit Three.js r186** (recheck the current stable release during implementation) for each class's constructor arguments, scope constants, mutable state, runtime update behavior, serialization, child links, renderer/camera dependencies and supported shader stages.
2. Add **paired default exporter serialization and loader resolution** for safe, well-defined variants:
   - `IndexNode`: explicitly allowlist valid index scopes; preserve scope and native Three.js per-draw/vertex/instance semantics.
   - `FrontFacingNode`: reconstruct ordinary instances without changing front/back-facing behavior or accidentally replacing them with a shared singleton.
   - `ScreenNode`: explicitly allowlist coordinate/size/viewport scopes, preserve live renderer/frame updates where applicable, and avoid serializing display dimensions as frozen literals.
   - `ViewportDepthNode`: preserve valid scopes and optional linked input(s), distinguish camera/renderer-context dependencies, and only support modes whose meaning is preserved by the actual Three.js runtime.
3. Reuse Three.js classes, `serialize()`, `deserialize()` and `getSerializeChildren()` where appropriate. Do not duplicate shader calculations or introduce file-supplied code.
4. If any scope or mode needs ambiguous camera/renderer ownership, unavailable context or disproportionate complexity, **defer that mode explicitly**, with the exact name, reason and a future adapter/binding approach. Do not silently change its semantics or claim universal support.
5. Preserve existing shared TSL singleton identity and protections. Invalid/unknown scopes, extra or broken links and unsupported variants must **fail clearly on export**; any loader reconstruction failure must atomically retain the entire ordinary glTF material as Draft v2.0 requires.

## Context

- [Draft v2.0 specification](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [Current coverage matrix](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md)
- [Default serializer](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/defaultNodeSerializer.ts)
- [Default resolver](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/defaultNodeResolver.ts)
- [Real integration tests](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)
- [Three.js r186 source](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/tree/r186/src/nodes)
- Previous incremental coverage work: #15, #17, #19, #21.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Audit all four classes and document explicitly supported vs deferred scope/mode variants.
- [ ] Implement paired default serializer/resolver adapters for all feasible variants; retain existing singleton behavior and shared graph references.
- [ ] Add real GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader round-trip tests for each newly supported class, including correct node identity, graph connections, default/explicit scopes and material entrypoints.
- [ ] Compare Three.js shader generation and/or native runtime update behavior where feasible, especially renderer/viewport/camera-dependent modes; do not assume that JSON equality establishes runtime equivalence.
- [ ] Add negative tests for unsupported scopes, malformed links, invalid graph references, inappropriate renderer dependencies and full ordinary material fallback.
- [ ] Update the coverage matrix and loader/exporter READMEs with exact supported scopes, renderer-context limitations and reasons for deferred cases.
- [ ] Keep the Draft v2.0 specification unchanged and v1.0 support removed; no arbitrary JavaScript, GLSL or WGSL embedded in glTF.
- [ ] Run the full test suite, loader/exporter/demo builds, demo typecheck, and `git diff --check`; report actual results and skips.

## Optional validation

Browser/WebGPU visual smoke tests of front-facing, screen-coordinate and viewport-depth nodes with a real camera and renderer. If not performed, document that Node-side shader generation does not prove GPU pixel behavior.

## Required post-merge verification
